paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Miriam and Aaron wanted to be heard, and it came out as criticism of their own brother. They said, "Does the LORD speak only through Moses?" and the LORD heard this (Numbers 12:2). Nothing said in the wilderness, in a tent or in a group chat stays hidden from Him.

Then look at who Moses is. The text says he "was a very humble man, more so than any man on the face of the earth" (Numbers 12:3). He never defended himself in this passage. The LORD called him "My servant Moses" and said, "he is faithful in all My house" (Numbers 12:7). I think that's the lesson, baker: you don't have to fight for your own place when God is the One who sets it.

And watch what Moses does when his sister is in trouble. He cries out, "O God, please heal her!" (Numbers 12:13). The same brother they criticized is the one who prays for them. I'll be honest, I want a heart like that, a heart that prays for the people who talked about it behind its back.
